en:
חֶרֶס I m. (Biblical Hebrew חֶרֶשׂ; חרס to be rough; to scrape)
1) common earthware. כלי ח׳ earthen vessel. Kelim III, 1 (ed. Dehr. חרש); and see from—Ib. 4 היה בה ח׳ if there remained of it a (sound) piece large enough to contain &c.—Midrash Tanḥuma Sh’laḥ. 1 (reference. to חֶרֶשׁ, Joshua II, 1) קרי ביה ח׳ read it ḥeres (with earthware, in the disguise of potters); Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 16, beginning חרשׂ; and from—Esp. (see חַסְפָּא) potsherd. Yerushalmi Nedarim I, 37ᵃ top; Yerushalmi Nazir I, beginning 51ᵃ והתני … לא חספא did not Bar K. say, ḥeres is a substitute for ḥerem (חֵרֶם)? now, does not this mean a sherd (which has no reference to anything forbidden either as sacred or as doomed to destruction)?; see next word—plural חֲרָסִים, חֲרָסִין. Kelim III, 4. Ib. IX, 5 (Arukh חֲרָשִׂין); and e.—Chagigah 13ᵇ (explained בזק, Ezekiel I, 14) כאור … מבין הח׳ like the flames from between the perforated earthen pieces (used in smelting gold).

כַּבְכָּב, (כַּפְכָּף) m. (reduplic. of כבב or כפף, see כְּבַב) an arched round vessel. Kelim II, 3 כ׳ שעשאו לסל הפת a kabkab which was intended for a cover for the bread-basket (and not as a receptacle). Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 5 כסוי כ׳ וכסוי אלפס ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (ed. only כסוי אלפס) the lid of a k. and that of a pot. Ib. 8 העשוי לכך ולכך כגון הכ׳ וכ׳ Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim III, 1 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) and oth. כנכב) a vessel made for both purposes (for liquids and for solid food), e.g. the k., the stew-pot &c.

comments.en: If the hive was complete, and so too in the case of a basket or a skin-bottle, and a sheretz was within it the oven remains clean. If the sheretz was in the oven, any food in the hive remain clean. If a hole was made in it: A vessel that is used for food must have a hole large enough for olives to fall through, If it is used for liquids the hole must be large enough for liquids to pass into it, And if it is used for either it is subjected to the greater restriction: the hole need only be large enough for liquids to pass into it.
comments.he: הָיְתָה שְׁלֵמָה, וְכֵן הַקֻּפָּה, וְכֵן הַחֵמֶת, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הַתַּנּוּר טָהוֹר. הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, אֳכָלִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ טְהוֹרִין. נִקְּבוּ, הֶעָשׂוּי לְאֳכָלִין, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים. הֶעָשׂוּי לְמַשְׁקִין, שִׁעוּרָן בְּמַשְׁקִים. הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ, מַטִּילִים אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ, בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה:

comments.en: If there was a hole in the "eye" of an oven, the minimum size [for it to leave the category of being tightly closed] is the circumference of a burning spindle staff that can enter and come out [without being extinguished]. Rabbi Judah says: one that is not burning. If the hole appeared at its side, the minimum size must be that of the circumference of a spindle staff that can enter and come out while it is not burning. Rabbi Judah says: while burning. Rabbi Shimon says: if the hole is in the middle its size must be such that a spindle staff can enter it, but if it was at the side it need only be such as the spindle staff cannot actually enter. And similarly he used to rule concerning the stopper of a jar in which a hole appeared: the minimum size is the circumference of the second knot in an oat stalk. If the hole was in the middle the stalk should be able to enter, and if at the side it need not be able to enter. And similarly he used to rule concerning large stone jars in the stoppers of which appeared a hole. The minimum size is the circumference of the second knot in a reed. If the hole was in the middle the reed must be able to enter it, and if it was at the side the reed need not be able to enter it. When is this so? When the jars were made for wine, but if they were made for other liquids, if they have even the smallest hole, they are unclean. When is this so? When the holes were not made by a person, but if they were made by a person, if they have even the smallest hole, they are unclean. If a hole appeared [in other vessels its prescribed size ] is as follows: if the vessel was used for food, [the hole must be one] through which olives can fall out; if for liquids, one that lets out liquids; If for either, the greater restriction is imposed [even with regard to the issue of] a tightly fitting cover [the size of the hole need only be] one that admits a liquid.
comments.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁנִּקַּב מֵעֵינוֹ, שִׁעוּרוֹ מְלֹא כוּשׁ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹלֵק. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁלֹּא דוֹלֵק. נִקַּב מִצִּדּוֹ, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא כוּשׁ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא שֶׁלֹּא דוֹלֵק. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דּוֹלֵק. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס. מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס. וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בִּמְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה, שִׁעוּרָהּ מְלֹא מִיצָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל שִׁיפוֹן. מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס. מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס. וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בַּחֲצָבִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁנִּקְּבוּ, שִׁעוּרָם מְלֹא מִיצָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קָנֶה. מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס. מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לְיַיִן, אֲבָל אִם נַעֲשׂוּ לִשְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין, אֲפִלּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא, טְמֵאִים. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשׂוּ בִידֵי אָדָם. אֲבָל אִם נַעֲשׂוּ בִידֵי אָדָם, אֲפִלּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא, טְמֵאִים. נִקְּבוּ, הֶעָשׂוּי לָאֳכָלִים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים. הֶעָשׂוּי לְמַשְׁקִים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּמַשְׁקִים. הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ, מַטִּילִים אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ, בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל וּבְכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה:
כאשר בונים מקווה, אפשר להיעזר בברזלים לחיזוק הבטון, למרות שבתנאים מסוימים הם יכולים לקבל טומאה, מפני שכל מה שמחובר לקרקע ואינו כלי, בטל לקרקע.

sections.en: The size of a hole that renders an earthen vessel clean:If the vessel was made for food, the hole must be big enough for olives [to fall through]. If it was used for liquids it suffices for the hole to be big enough for liquids [to go through it]. And if it was used for both, we apply the greater stringency, that olives must be able to fall through.
sections.he: שִׁעוּר כְּלִי חֶרֶס לִטַּהֵר, הֶעָשׂוּי לְאֳכָלִין, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְזֵיתִים. הֶעָשׂוּי לְמַשְׁקִין, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְמַשְׁקִין. הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ, מַטִּילִין אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ בְזֵיתִים:

en: אָפוּן m. bean (compare אפול section (Parashah) see אֲפוֹלִים). Yerushalmi Yoma IV, 43ᶜ bottom of page עד כא׳ only the size of a bean; see חָאפוּן. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. III, 43ᵃ bottom of page וכא׳ היה had the shape of a bean.—plural אֲפוּנִים, אֲפוּנִין. Kelim III, 2 א׳ הגמלונין Arukh, Manuscript Munich (ed. הגמלנים) large beans; see גַּמְלוֹן. Shabbat XXI, 3 (143ᵃ) שער של א׳ (Manuscript L. עפ׳; ed. Soncino פולין) the silique of the bean. Teb. Yom I, 5; and from

טָפִי m. (= טְפִיחַ I, see טְפֵי II) [dripper,] vessel with a narrow neck. Kelim II, 3 ט׳ שהתקינו לענבים a pitcher which was made with the intention of using it for grapes. Ib. III, 2. Negaim XII, 5 טָפְיוֹ (Rabbenu Shimshon and l. תָּפְיוֹ) man’s oil vessels.

נָא II m. (also adverb)(b. h.;
1) hurried, half-done. Pesachim 41ᵃ bottom of page אכלו נא if he ate it (the Passover lamb) half-done. Ib.ᵇ ישנו בבל תאכל נא is subject to the law (Shemot XII, 9) &c. Tosefta Makkot IV (III), 1, contradistinguished to חַי. Menachot 78ᵇ מצה נא, see הַיָנָא; and from

—2) slender, fine, brittle. — plural נָאִין; f. נָאוֹת. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 9 [read with Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim III, 2:] הוסקו והנאין (= והן נאין) if the vessels were heated but turned out brittle. B. Bath, 97ᵇ (explained פיטסות, ib. VI, 2) נאות ומגופרות thin, but lined with pitch; Tosefta ib. VI, 3.

צִרְצוּר, צִירְ׳ m. (compare צְרוֹר II) a stone vessel containing a strainer and having an indented (comb-like) rim; a sort of cooler. Kelim II, 8 המסרק של צ׳ if an unclean object touches the ‘comb’ of a cooler; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 8; Tosefta Eduy. II, 1. Kelim III, 2. Mikvaot III, 3 המערה מן הצ׳ ומטיל וכ׳ if one pouring water out of a cooler throws water out in several places. Pirkei Avot Zar. 73ᵃ המערה … מצי׳ קטן וכ׳ if one pours forbidden wine from a small cooler into the wine pit. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 28ᵈ top והיה שם צ׳ וכ׳ and there stood a pitcher full of Ammonite wine; Bavli Sanhedrin 106ᵃ צרצורי (correct accordingly); Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 20; Midrash Tanḥuma Balaḳ 18; Yalkut Bamidbar 771 (ed. Salon. סרסור, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) to Sanhedrin l. common gender. note 1). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 98 [read:] אפי׳ היה צ׳ של מים בצדו וכ׳ even if a pitcher of water had stood by his side, he would have been unable to put his hand forth &c.—plural צִרְצוּרִין. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 9.

שִׁיקּוּר II m. name of an earthen vessel (probably a tumbler that cannot stand, see Shabbat 104ᵃ quot. section (Parashah) see שִׁקְרָא).—plural שִׁקּוּרִין. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 9 ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (oth. ed. שקורי; Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim III, 2 שִׁקּוּדִין).

comments.en: The lattice [cover] of a stone water cooler (tzartzur): Rabbi Eliezer says it cannot impart impurity through its airspace, and the Sages say, it does impart impurity through its airspace. If it was [able to be] used for this and for that, such as for a kavkav (an arched round vessel), and for a stewpot, and for a cooking pot, they impose upon it the stringencies [both] for receiving [impurity] and for causing impurity to issue forth upon others. [For example, it may receive impurity if it has a hole] large enough for water to seep through, but it itself is only pure [when it has a hole] through which olives can fall. Wineskins: Their minimum size [for being susceptible to impurity is an opening large enough] for liquids [to pass through], and Rabbi Shimon says, for seedlings. A damaged jar (gis'terah): Its minimum size is for liquids [to pass through, and a petikah (see Zar Zahav), behold, that is pure. A Galilean oil cruse that they use to transport oil to a bathhouse, and a stone water cooler and a wooden bowl: Before they are fired they are pure. An earthenware shard that became separated from a jar or from a cooking pot: If it can hold [liquid] of the minimum amount, it is impure, and if not, it is pure. [If] it was punctured and they covered it with pitch, it [remains] pure, for an earthenware vessel that is pure for [even] one hour will never again become impure.
comments.he: מסרק של צרצור ר' אליעזר אומר אין מטמא באויר וחכ"א מטמא באויר העשוי לכך ולכך כגון הכבכב והאילפס והקדרה מטילין אותו לחומר להכניס ולהוציא טומאה לאחרים ככונס משקה אבל הוא עצמו אין טהור אלא במוציא זיתים בלבד. נבלי יין שיעורן במשקין ור"ש אומר בזרעונין <שעורו במשקין ור"ש אומר בזרעונין> נסטרא שיעורה במשקה והעתיקה ה"ז טהור הפכין הגלילין שמוליכין בהן שמן למרחץ והצרצורין והשקורין עד שלא הוסקו טהורין ומשהוסקו טמאין והסקין והנאין טמאין חרש שפירש מן חבית ומן הקדרה אם מקבל כשיעור טמא אם לאו טהור נקב ועשאו בזפת טהור שכלי חרש שטהור שעה אחת אין לו טומאה לעולם.

sections.en: A jar: the size of the hole must be such that a dried fig [will fall through], the words of Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Judah said: walnuts. Rabbi Meir said: olives. A stew-pot or a cooking pot: such that olives [will fall through]. A bucket and a pitcher: such that oil [will fall through]. A tzartzur: such that water [will fall through]. Rabbi Shimon says: in the case of all three, [the hole] must be such that seedlings [will fall through]. A lamp: the size of the hole must be such that oil [will fall through]. Rabbi Eliezer says: such that a small perutah [will fall through]. A lamp whose nozzle has been removed is clean. And one made of earth whose nozzle has been burned by the wick is also clean.
sections.he: חָבִית, שִׁעוּרָהּ בִּגְרוֹגָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בֶּאֱגוֹזִים. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, בְּזֵיתִים. הַלְּפָס וְהַקְּדֵרָה, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים. הַפַּךְ וְהַטְּפִי, שִׁעוּרָן בְּשָׁמֶן. וְהַצַּרְצוּר, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְמָיִם. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שְׁלָשְׁתָּן בְּזֵרְעוֹנִין. נֵר, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְשָׁמֶן. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בִּפְרוּטָה קְטַנָּה. נֵר שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיו, טָהוֹר. וְשֶׁל אֲדָמָה שֶׁהֻסַּק פִּיו בַּפְּתִילָה, טָהוֹר:

en:
שָׁבַר I (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to break. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 41ᵈ (play on אכל תשברו, Devarim II, 6) באכל תִּשְׁבְּרוֹ האכלתו שְׁבַרְתּוֹ with food break him (his ill-will); when thou hast given him to eat, thou hast broken him; אם היה קשה עליך באכל תשברו וכ׳ if he is hard on thee, break him with food, and if not (if thou succeedest not with food), heap silver upon him; Yerushalmi Shabbat I, 3ᶜ bottom of page Midrash Tanḥuma Sh’laḥ. 9 נתכוונו … לִשְׁבּוֹר לבן וכ׳ the spies intended to break the heart (courage) of the Israelites (reference. to ויניאו, Bamidbar XXXII, 9). Tosefta Bava Metzia II, 26 אוהבו … כדי לשבור את לבו if a friend requires help for loading, and an enemy for unloading (to relieve the broken down beast of burden), it is commended to help the enemy in order to break his heart (hatred); (Bava Metzia 32ᵇ כדי לכוף את יצרו). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Eth Korb., p. 59ᵇ נטל את הטבלא … ושְׁבָרָהּ he took the plate … and shattered it. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 18 (reference. to Psalms LXXVII, 7) נזכרת אני את השברים שהיית שׁוֹבֵר וכ׳ I remember the breaks with which thou brokest (the calamities with which thou didst visit) the empires for me by night; בא … שָׁבַרְתָּ וכ׳ Sennacherib came upon me, thou brokest him at night (see infra Hof.); and see from—Yerushalmi Sheviit VIII, beginning 37ᵈ כל מדרש שאתה דורש ושׁוֹבֵר וכ׳ a textual interpretation which you introduce, and by which you break (upset partially) a previous interpretation of the same verse, is no legitimate interpretation. Midrash Tanḥuma Vayera 13 סופו … שובר את ראשו the end of the verse breaks (contradicts) its beginning. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VII, 9 (explained דתבריא, Daniel III, 2) the scholars (scholastici) are called d’thabraya (see תְּבַר), שהם שׁוֹבְרִים הדברים because they break (twist out of joint) the words (of the law).—Part. pass. שָׁבוּר, f. שְׁבוּרָה having a broken limb, injured. Bava Metzia I, 4 רצין … אחר צבי ש׳ running … after a wounded deer. Ib. 94ᵇ ש׳ ומתה a borrowed animal that was injured or that died. Ib. נשבעין על הש׳
must make oath concerning an injured animal in their charge; and from—2) (denominative of שׁוֹבֵר) to give a receipt; to acknowledge payment; to acquit. Tosefta Ketubot IV, 11 שָׁבְרָה לו (על) מקצת כתובתה שברה לו אל כולה if she gave him a receipt for a portion of her jointure, she has released him of all obligations of the marriage contract. Ib. IX, 1 כונסה … והיא שׁוֹבֶרֶת לו וכ׳ he marries her and divorces her (and remarries her), and she gives him a receipt for her jointure (by which act the mortgage on the entire estate is cancelled); Yerushalmi ib. VIII, 32ᵇ bottom of page; Yerushalmi Yevamot IV, 5ᵈ; and from

Piël - שִׁבֵּר to break. Shabbat 105ᵇ המקרע … והמְשַׁבֵּר כליו וכ׳ he who in his anger tears his garment or breaks his vessels, … let him be in thy sight like an idolater; and from—Part. pass. מְשׁוּבָּר. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 17 (reference. to Job I, 15) מש׳ ומלוקה היה he (that escaped) was broken of limbs and smitten; Ruth Rabbah to I, 5; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 17 מוּשְׁבָּר; Yalkut Job 892 מושבר.

Hof. - הוּשְׁבַּר to be broken. sections.en: A jar that had a hole and was mended with pitch and then was broken again: If the fragment that was mended with the pitch can hold a quarter of a log it is unclean, since the designation of a vessel has never ceased to be applied to it. A potsherd that had a hole and was mended with pitch, it is clean though it can contain a quarter of a log, because the designation of a vessel has ceased to be applied to it.

—2) (of lower animals) to breed, increase (see טָפֵל). Kiddushin 80ᵃ ושרצים … מִיטַּפְּלִין שם vermin and frogs breed in the house.

Pu. - מְטוּפָּל (denominative of טָפֵל) burdened with a large family. Taanit 16ᵃ, sq. מט׳ ואין לו one having a large family with no means of support.

comments.en: If one of them [i.e. the props] was removed, the remaining ones contract impurity by contact but not through air-space, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean. If originally he made two props, one opposite the other, they contract impurity by contact and through air-space; the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean. If they were more than three fingerbreadths high, the parts that are three fingerbreadths high and below contract impurity by contact and through air-space but the parts that are more than three fingerbreadths high contract impurity by contact and not through air-space; the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean. If they were withdrawn from the rim [of the stove], the parts which are within three fingerbreadths contract impurity by contact and through air-space, and those parts that are removed more than three fingerbreadths contract impurity by contact but not through air-space, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean.
comments.he: נִטַּל אַחַד מֵהֶן, מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָם מִטַּמְּאִים בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר. עָשָׂה שְׁנַיִם, זֶה כְנֶגֶד זֶה, מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר. הָיוּ גְבוֹהִין מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִשָּׁלֹשׁ וּלְמַטָּן מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, מִשָּׁלֹשׁ וּלְמַעְלָן מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר. הָיוּ מְשׁוּכִים מִן הַשָּׂפָה, בְּתוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, חוּץ מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָם מִטַּמְּאִים בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר:

sections.en: If a jar was about to be cracked but was strengthened with cattle dung, although the potsherds would fall apart were the dung to be removed, it is unclean, because the designation of vessel never ceased to apply. If it was broken and some of its pieces were stuck together again, or if he brought other pieces of clay from elsewhere, and it was also lined with cattle dung, even though the potsherds hold together when the dung is removed, it is clean, because the designation of vessel ceased to apply. If it contained one potsherd that could hold a quarter of a log, all its parts contract impurity by contact, but that potsherd contracts impurity through its air-space.
sections.he: חָבִית שֶׁנִּתְרוֹעֲעָה וּטְפָלָהּ בִּגְלָלִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל אֶת הַגְּלָלִים וְהַחֲרָסִים נוֹפְלִים, טְמֵאָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא בָטַל שֵׁם כְּלִי מֵעָלֶיהָ. נִשְׁבְּרָה וְדִבֵּק מִמֶּנָּה חַרְסִית, אוֹ שֶׁהֵבִיא חַרְסִית מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וּטְפָלָן בִּגְלָלִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל הַגְּלָלִים וְהַחֲרָסִין עוֹמְדִים, טְהוֹרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל שֵׁם כְּלִי מֵעָלֶיהָ. הָיָה בָהּ חֶרֶס מַחֲזִיק רְבִיעִית, כֻּלָּהּ מִטַּמָּא בְמַגָּע, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר:

en: חִידּוּק, חִדּ׳, הִ׳ m. (חָדַק, הָ׳) that which is sqeezed in to fill a gap, repair, insertion. Chullin 57ᵇ one who had a hole in the (fractured) scull, ועשו לו ח׳ של קרויה וכ׳ ed. יָקָר m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.)
1) heavy; dear, precious, worthy; honored. Tosefta Bava Kamma IX, 12 המתבייש מן הי׳ who is put to shame by a person of high dignity (opposed פגום).—plural יְקָרִים, יְקָרִין. Bava Batra 100ᵇ; Megillah 23ᵇ (address to mourners) עמדו י׳ עמודו וכ׳ stand up, dear friends, stand up &c. Menachot 44ᵃ דמיו י׳ its price is high; and from—Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 2 היְקָרִין Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim III, 5 (ed. היקירן, הייקרין) the heavy earthen vessels used for boiling pitch.—Fem. יְקָרָה, plural יְקָרוֹת. —2) (noun) precious object, prize; choice. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 67 (reference. to Mishlei XII, 27) כדי … שהוא יְקָרוֹ של עולם וכ׳ in order that Jacob might come who is the choice of the world &c.; ib. שאינם נוטלים מן יְקָרָם שלעתיד לכוא וכ׳ that they shall receive in this world nothing of their prize reserved for the hereafter; Yalkut ib. 115, see חָרַץ.—plural יְקָרוֹת. 1) to heap, pile. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 100 (reference. to כריתי, Breishit L, 5) הרבה ממון תַּכְרֶה עליה much money shalt thou pile up (give me) for it (the grave); (some ed. הכרה Jacob piled up in settling with Esau). Ib. הִכְרֵתִי (correct הִכְרֵיתִי); see כְּרִי; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 1 וכל ממון שהיה לו ה׳ וכ׳ (not מסר לו) and he (Jacob) piled up whatever money he had to place it before Esau &c.

—2) to invite to a banquet;
3) (with play on כרת) to excise, to destroy. Sanhedrin 20ᵃ; Yalkut Samuel 142 (reference. to להברות, II Samuel III, 35, where Raba had before him a K’thib. להכרות) כתיב להכרות … בתחלה להַכְרוֹתוֹ וכ׳ it is written l’hakhroth (to entertain) and read l’habroth (see בָּרָה): originally they came with the intention of destroying him (for the murder of Abner), and finally (when convinced of his innocence) they came to comfort him; [Yalk. Manuscript to Samuel l. common gender., quoted in Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) Sanhedrin l. common gender. note 9: כתיב לִבְרוֹת וקרינן להַבְרוֹת בתחלה לברות וכ׳ it is written libroth (to pierce, compare Ezekiel XXIII, 47), and we read l’habroth &c.].

קֵרוּיָה, קֵיר׳ f. (see קָרָא I) pumpkin-shell used as a drawing vessel, cooler. Shabbat XVII, 6 (125ᵃ) האבן שבקי׳ (Yerushalmi ed. קֵירוּיָא; Manuscript Munich קֵרוּיָיא) the stone which is put into a drawing vessel (to weight it); ib. 125ᵇ שבקרויה (Manuscript Munich שבקריא, correct accordingly). Chullin 57ᵇ (Manuscript Munich קרא); Kelim III, 5; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 3, see חִידּוּק; and e.

רָעַע (Biblical Hebrew) [to bring in close contact, see רֵיעַ,]
1) to strike against, shatter, impair. —Part. pass. רָעוּעַ; f. רְעוּעָה; plural רְעוּעִים, רְעוּעִין; רְעוּעוֹת impaired, defective; in a ruinous state, threatening, opposed בריא sound. Kiddushin 39ᵇ סולם ר׳ a broken ladder. Kelim III, 5 הר׳ a cracked vessel. Taanit 20ᵇ מפולת שאמרו בריאות ולא ר׳ the falling of houses which they mention (ib. III, 4) means the falling of sound buildings, but not of such as were out of repair; and from

—2) (neut. verb) רַע, imperf. יֵרַע to be injurious, evil; רע ל־ to grieve, displease. Bava Metzia 84ᵇ בני אל ירע לך my son, let it not grieve thee; and e.

Piël - רֵעַע to shatter, break.—Part. pass. מְרוֹעָע; f. מְרוֹעַעַת; plural מְרוֹעָעִים, מְרוֹעָעִין; מְרוֹעָעוֹת. Kohelet Rabbah to III, 2 השרוי בבית המר׳ he who dwells in a threatening house; Yerushalmi Shabbat II, 5ᵇ top מְרוֹעֲרַע (from רִעְרֵעַ). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 32 קנקנים מר׳, see קַנְקָן I. Yerushalmi Taanit III, 66ᵈ top מְרוֹעֲרָעִים threatening buildings; and from

Hithpaël - הִתְרָעֵעַ,

Nithpaël - נִתְרָעֵעַ, , Hithpol. הִתְרוֹעֵעַ, Nithpol. נִתְרוֹעֵעַ to be shaken, cracked, become defective. Menachot 53ᵇ (reference. to Jeremiah XI, 16) מקול מיליהן … נִיתְרָעֲעוּ דליותיהן וכ׳ from the sound of the words of the spies were the branches (young men) of Israel broken; Yalkut Jeremiah 289 נרתעו (read: נִתְרָעוּ). Sotah 48ᵃ (play on ערה, Zephaniah II, 14) אפי׳ בית … מִתְרוֹעֵעַ even a house which lies in a thicket of cedars will be shaken; Yalkut Isaiah 292 מתנועע (correct accordingly). Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 27ᵈ bottom of page לכיפה … כיון שנִתְרוֹעֲעָה אחת מהן נִתְרוֹעֲעוּ כולן like a heap of stones, when one of them is shaken (disturbed), all of them are shaken; Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan III, 83ᶜ שנִתְרַעְרְעָה … נִתְרַעְרְעוּ (from רערע); Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 100 וכולה מִתְרוֹעַעַת; and e.

Hifil - הֵרַע
1) to shake, impair. Yerushalmi Sheviit X, 39ᵈ top מֵירַע כוחן it impairs their prerogatives; ib. מוֹרַע (from יָרַע). Yerushalmi Pesachim VII, 34ᵈ top שהוֹרַעְתָּ כחו וכ׳ whose standing thou declarest impaired in the case of an ascertained uncleanness. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 8 הֵרֵעוּ לנפשם they did harm to themselves; and e.—V. הֲרָעָה.

—2) to be evil; ה׳ ל־ to displease. Midrash Tanḥuma Sh’laḥ 5; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 167 וה׳ לאביו and it displeased his father; and e.—[
3) to join, combine, see רָעָהPiël]

Hof. - הוּרַע , or הוֹרַע (from יָרַע) to be shaken, impaired. Kiddushin 20ᵇ, sq. ה׳ כחו his prerogative is impaired, see יָפֶה. Bava Kamma 44ᵃ; and from

comments.he:
82-83. שלחן שנטמא מטבילין אותו בזמנו ואפילו בשבת. וכ"ה ("שלחן") גם בד, בכי"ל ובקג"נ. וכ"ה בר"ח כ"ז א'. ובכי"ע בטעות: כלי שלהם שניטמא וכו'. ובכי"ע, קג"נ ור"ח: אפילו בשבת. ובמשנתנו פ"ג מ"ח: ואומרין להם הזהרו שלא תגעו בשלחן ובמנורה וכו'. ופירשו בבבלי כ"ו ב' משום שכתוב בהם תמיד, ואסור לטלטלם ממקומם (עיין בהשגות הראב"ד כלים פ"ג ה"א) כדי להטבילם. ובשולחן, אעפ"י שהיו מוציאין אותו ברגל מן ההיכל, מ"מ צריך ליזהר שלא יגעו בו ויטמאו גם את הלחם. ומפרש כאן שאם נטמא מטבילין אותו (עיין בבלי פסחים ק"ט ב') בזמנו וכו'. ועיין מ"ש להלן.
ובירושלמי פ"ג ה"ח, ע"ט ע"ד: תני שולחן שניטמא מטבילין אותו בזמנו אפילו בשבת דברי ר' מאיר. וחכמים אומרים מיד וכו'. ועיי"ש בגליון הש"ס ובפי' הרידב"ז. והנכון הוא בח"ד כאן, בנוע"י ובס' ניר, והכוונה שלדעת ר' מאיר מטבילין אותו בזמנו דווקא, כלומר בשעה שמסלקים את הישן, ואפילו בשבת שאסור לטבול התירו, משום שאין שבות במקדש. וחכמים סוברים שמטבילים אותו מיד, ביום שניטמא. והמשך הירושלמי מבואר בח"ד ובנועם ירושלמי שם, ועיי"ש בירושלמי שפירשוהו בניטמא בספק טומאת משקין.

sections.en: One who lines a sound vessel: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon say: [the lining] contracts impurity. But the sages say: a lining over a sound vessel is not susceptible to impurity, and only one over a cracked vessel is susceptible. And the same dispute applies to the hoop of a pumpkin shell.
sections.he: הַטּוֹפֵל כְּלִי חֶרֶס הַבָּרִיא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַמְּאִים. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַטּוֹפֵל אֶת הַבָּרִיא, טָהוֹר. וְאֶת הָרָעוּעַ, טָמֵא. וְכֵן בְּחִדּוּק הַקֵּרוּיָה:

en: חִיבּוּר, חִבּוּר m. (חָבַר) junction, connection. Kelim III, 6 אינה ח׳ is not considered a connection (touching the stopper by an unclean person &c. does not affect the contents of the cask). Ib. XVIII, 2; Shabbat 44ᵇ; 46ᵃ.—Pirkei Avot Zar. 56ᵇ, and e. נצוק ח׳ the jet produced by pouring out is a connection (the liquid at one end, if touched by a gentile &c., affects that in the vessel); Toharot VIII, 9; and see from—Yerushalmi Sotah VIII, 22ᵈ אין … ח׳ לעיר we do not consider it as connected with the town (as regards Sabbath limits). Yerushalmi Kilayim IX, end, 32ᵈ ח׳ לבגד considered as connected (woven) with the garment; and from

יַבְלִית f. (see יַבְלָא) a pulp made of Cynodon leaves and used for lining large water vessels. Kelim III, 6 (ed. Dehr. יְבָלִית); Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 2 יַבְלוּת (see Löw Löw, Aramäische Pflanzennamen, Leipzig 1881 p. 186).

פִּיטּוּס, פִּיטָּס (frequently פִּיטּוּם, פִּיטָּם) common gender. (פטס to expand, compare פָּטַם 2)
1) a large cylindrical vessel, cask or tub of earthen material (corresp. to πίθος, and to dolium; see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 18583 Engl. ed., section (Parashah) see Dolium). Bava Metzia IV, 12 (60ᵃ) התגר … פיטם אחד (Bavli ed. פיטום; Yerushalmi ed. Venice and Mishnah ed. Nap. פיטס; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 400) a merchant may buy wine from several presses and put it into one cask. Ketubot 111ᵇ in the days to come מביא ענבה … כפ׳ גדול one will bring in one cluster of grapes on a wagon or in a boat and place it in a corner of his house, and take his supply of wine from it, as if it were a large jar; Sifré Devarim 317 כשותה מן הפיטום; Yalkut ib. 944 ומסתפק והולך מן הפטים (read כמן הפ׳); Yalkut Breishit 160 בפ׳ גדול (correct accordingly). Rosh Hashanah III, 7 (27ᵇ) הפיטם (Bavli ed. הפיטס; Manuscript Munich הפיטם, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note). Tosefta Oholot X, 3 פ׳ שהוא עומד וכ׳ a piṭṭus (pithos) standing in a room and reaching from the floor to the ceiling. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma IV, 16 פיטים שקירו וכ׳ (correct accordingly) a large tub to which one made a cover to use it as a stove, and which he plastered over with clay. Yerushalmi Beitzah III, 62ᵃ top צד הוא בפיטס he may catch an animal (on the Holy Day) by chasing it into a tub; Yerushalmi Shabbat III, 14ᵃ bottom of page בפיתם (read ס …). Tosefta T’bul Yom II, 3 פִּיתוֹס.—plural פִּיטְּסִין, פִּטְּ׳. Kelim III, 6 שטופלין בה הפ׳ (Arukh הפדיסין) wherewith they line the tubs. Beitzah 15ᵇ הללו בעלי פ׳ those (the first to leave the lecture room) are owners of tubs of wine, contradistinguished to חבית &c.

—2) a vessel made of brittle clay and requiring lining.—plural פִּיטְּסוֹת. Bava Batra VI, 2 (93ᵇ) קנקנים בשרון … פיטסות למאה (Manuscript Hamburg and R. פּוֹטְסוֹת; Mishnah ed. פִּיטַסְיָאוֹת, Yerushalmi ed. פִּיטְסָאוֹת) if a man buys jugs (קנקנים) in Sharon, he must accept ten thin jugs for every hundred; ib. 97ᵇ, explained נאות ומגופרות, see נָא II; Tosefta ib. VI, 3, sq. פוטסות ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (oth. ed. פוניסות, פינוסות, correct accordingly).

sections.en: As to dog's tooth which which they line large jars: anything that touches it becomes unclean. The plug of a jar is not regarded as connected. That which touches the lining of an oven is unclean.
sections.he: יַבְּלִית שֶׁטּוֹפְלִין בָּהּ הַפִּטָּסִין, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהּ, טָמֵא. מְגוּפַת חָבִית, אֵינָהּ חִבּוּר. הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּטִפּוּלוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, טָמֵא:

en: חַרְסִית II f. (חֶרֶס I) potter’s clay, clay-ground. Ma'aser Sheni V, 1 בח׳ must be marked off with burned clay. Chullin VI, 7 בח׳; ib. 88ᵃ שחיקת ח׳ powdered burned clay. Kelim III, 7; and from—[Tosefta Terumot IX, 3 חרסיות, see חָסִית I.]

טָהוֹר, טְהוֹרָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; next word)
1) clean, pure; not subject to levitical uncleanness. Bava Metzia 86ᵃ שגופך ט׳ … נשמתך בט׳ (Manuscript בטהרה) thy body is pure, and thy soul expired with (the word) ‘pure’; Sanhedrin 68ᵃ.—Kiddushin 70ᵇ וסימניך טמא טמא ט׳ ט׳ and the sign (by which to remember which of the two families is of unblemished descent) is, that with the name of an unclean animal (raven) is unclean, that with the name of a clean animal (dove) is clean; Bava Batra 91ᵃ. Kelim III, 7 ובחרסית ט׳ and the person that touches the clay is clean (not affected by levitical uncleanness). Ib. IV, 1 ט׳ is not subject to levitical uncleanness; and see from—דג ט׳, עוף; בהמה טהורה a fish, a bird, a domestic animal permitted to eat. Chullin XII, 2. Ib. IV, 3 בטהורה טהור if it occurs with an animal of the clean class, the person is levitically clean; and see from—plural טְהוֹרִים, טְהוֹרִין; טְהוֹרוֹת. Kelim II, 1 פשוטיהן ט׳ the flat-surfaced among them are not subject to uncleanness.—Berakhot 2ᵇ שהכהנים ט׳ וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. מטוהרים) when the purified priests enter &c. Bava Metzia 61ᵇ; and see from

קוּמְקוּם, קוּמְקוּמוֹס, קוּמְקוּמָס, קוּמְקְמ׳ m. (cucuma, κουκκούμιον, probably of Semitic origin; the form cucumus is not recorded in Lat. Dict.) kettle (smaller than מיחם). Kelim III, 7 קומקום Mishnah ed. (Talmud ed. קומקומוס; Maimonides קומקומס). Ib. XIV, 1 קומקום (ed. Dehr. קומקמוס). Tosefta Mikvaot VII (VIII), 1 קומקומים ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (correct accordingly; oth. ed. קומקום). Yerushalmi Pesachim VI, 33ᵃ bottom of page כבק׳ הזה אני יורד לו (not בק׳) I would meet him as if attacking him with a (boiling) kettle; מה הק׳ הזה וכ׳ as a kettle scalds and wounds and blackens (if thrown at a person), so would I &c.; Menachot 109ᵇ אני מטיל עליו ק׳ וכ׳ I would throw a kettle of hot water at him. Yerushalmi Beitzah II, 61ᶜ. Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 2; Yalkut Hosea 517 קוּמְקְמִין; and from—plural קוּמְקוֹמוֹסִין, קוּמְקְמוֹ׳, קוּמְקְמִין. Shabbat 151ᵃ קומקמוסין Manuscript Munich (ed. קומקמין). Pirkei Avot Zar. 75ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. V, end, 45ᵇ; Sifré Bamidbar 158 קוּמְקְמָסִים; Midrash Tanḥuma Chukat 2 קוּנְקוֹמוֹסִין (ed. Bub. קומקמסין).

sections.en: A cauldron which was lined with mortar or with potter's clay: That which touches the mortar is unclean; But that which touches the potter's clay is clean. A kettle which was punctured and the hole was stopped with pitch: Rabbi Yose rules that it is clean since it cannot hold hot water as cold. The same ruling he also gave concerning vessels made of pitch. Copper vessels which were lined with pitch the lining is clean, But if they are used for wine, it is unclean.
sections.he: מֵחַם שֶׁטְּפָלוֹ בְחֹמֶר וּבְחַרְסִית, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּחֹמֶר, טָמֵא. וּבַחַרְסִית, טָהוֹר. קוּמְקוּם שֶׁנִּקַּב וַעֲשָׂאוֹ בְזֶפֶת, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַחַמִּין כְּצוֹנֵן. וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בִּכְלֵי זֶפֶת. כְּלֵי נְחֹשֶׁת שֶׁזְּפָתָן, טְהוֹרִין. וְאִם לְיַיִן, טְמֵאִין:

en: מַשְׁפֵּךְ m. (שָׁפַךְ) funnel. Kelim III, 8. Tosefta Shabbat VIII (IX), 10; and from—Pirkei Avot V, 15 מ׳ a scholar that learns and forgets easily, compare מְשַׁמֶּרֶת.—plural מַשְׁפֵּכִים, מַשְׁפֵּכִין. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 7.

פָּקַק
1) to split, drive into, force open. Shabbat 155ᵇ ופוֹקֵק Manuscript Munich, see פָּקַס I.—Denom. פֶּקֶק.

—2) (denominative of פֶּקֶק; compare חָדַק and חֶדֶק) to insert a stop-gap; to stop. Kelim III, 8 משפך … שפְּקָקוֹ וכ׳ (not שפקקה) a funnel of wood or clay stopped off with pitch. Ib. XXVIII, 2 שהתקינו לָפוֹק בו את המרחץ (ed. Dehr. לפַקֵּק) (a shred) with which it was intended to fill up a gap in the bath. Yerushalmi Eruvin III, end, 25ᵇ צריך לפוק he must stop it off. Tosefta ib. XI (VII), 10 פּוֹקְקִין את הביב וכ׳ you may stop off a gutter with a cloth. Yerushalmi Shabbat XVII, 16ᵇ top קנה שהתקינו להיות פּוֹקֵק בו החלון a pole (with a coil or a board attached) which has been prepared to close the sky light with it; (Tosefta ib. XIV (XV), 3 להיות פותח ונועל בו), see פֶּקֶק. Bavli Shabbat 64ᵇ פוקק לה זוג בצוארה וכ׳ he may muffle the bell on an animal’s neck (that it should not ring), and walk with it &c.; and from—Part. pass. פָּקוּק; plural פְּקוּקִין. Ib. אע"פ שפ׳ nor should the animal be led out with a bell, even if it is muffled. Yerushalmi Terumot VIII, 45ᵈ מכוסה ואינו פ׳ if the bottle is covered but not stopped; Tosefta Terumot VII, 16 [read:] מכוסין ואינן פקוקין (and correct the entire passage in conformity with Yerushalmi l. common gender.), see פֶּקֶק.

Piël - פִּיקֵּק same, see supra.—[Tosefta Ma'asrot I, 5 מפקק ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta), see פָּקַס II.]

Hithpaël - הִתְפַּקֵּק,

Nithpaël - נִתְפַּקֵּק
1) to be shaken, loosened. Berakhot 28ᵇ שיִתְפַּקְּקוּ, see פִּקְפֵּק. Midrash Tanḥuma Aḥăré 8 בשעה שנִתְפַּקְּקָה הכהונה וכ׳ when the priesthood in the hands of Aaron became shaky (was disputed); see פִּקְפֵּק.

—2) to be stopped. Yevamot 63ᵇ מִתְפַּקְּקִין, see פִּקְפֵּק.

sections.en: A jar which which was pierced and the hole stopped up with more pitch than was necessary: That which touches the needed portion is unclean, But that which touches the unneeded portion is clean. Pitch which dripped upon a jar, that which touches it is clean. A wooden or earthen funnel which was stopped up with pitch: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah says that it is unclean. Rabbi Akiva says that it is unclean when it is of wood and clean when it is of earthenware. Rabbi Yose says that both are clean.
